observations: All eight frozen identities produced complete causally valid control-treatment pairs with no censoring, retries, unknown token usage, or local failures.
Treatment improved macro Span-F1 from 3.0573% to 8.2243%, a gain of 5.1670 percentage points, and every frozen context-quality non-degradation check passed.
Treatment used 26,343 fewer logical cumulative model tokens than control, while every pair remained inside the 3,072-token treatment-over-control ceiling.
Valid context selections increased from three of eight in control to four of eight in treatment.
The four terminal-boundary pairs supplied all measured context-quality gain: terminal-phase Span-F1 increased by 10.3340 percentage points and valid selections increased from three to four.

The four effect-boundary pairs produced no valid context selections in either arm, but treatment used 29,575 fewer tokens in aggregate. This supports a possible exploration-control effect but does not show context-selection quality improvement at that phase.
Two effect-boundary pairs produced most of the aggregate token saving, so the efficiency result requires fresh replication before it is treated as stable.
inference: H67 is supported as a development hypothesis: one bounded, phase-tagged observable decision state can improve context selection and reduce aggregate token use under an 8K window. The evidence is phase-dependent and based on eight tasks, so the intervention must remain unchanged and face a larger fresh replication before small-window qualification or generalization.

selected_successor.name: universal decision-bound state fresh replication
selected_successor.mechanism: Replicate the frozen Round 48 decision-state/v1 intervention on a larger fresh, repository-stratified cohort without tuning the projection, prompts, thresholds, or scorer from the observed outcomes.

alternatives.name: effect-only readiness
alternatives.disposition: retained as a later mechanism study; the Round 48 effect stratum improved tokens but produced no valid selections

alternatives.name: terminal compact review
alternatives.disposition: retained as the phase that supplied the observed context-quality gain, but not substituted before replication

alternatives.name: no transferable observable-state gain
alternatives.disposition: not rejected beyond this development cohort

open_questions: Does the result replicate on a larger set of previously unused tasks and repositories?
Is the effect-phase token reduction stable, or dominated by task-specific variance?
Can effect-phase state produce valid final context selections with more continuation budget while preserving the frozen token objective?
Does the same state transition improve non-code retention tasks and other model families?
